newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean futures end mixed on uncertainty.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean futures end mixed on uncertainty.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mixed on Wednesday on uncertainties over the short-term market trend, traders said.
The key January 1997 contract ended at an intra-day high of 3,198 yuan ($385) per tonne, losing seven yuan. It opened at a low of 3,196.
March was unchanged at 3,240, May rose seven to 3,332, July up one to 3,371, September up two to 3,382 and November fell one to 3,399.
Combined volume rose to 11,200 tonnes from 11,100.
Traders said the flat performance of soybeans due to the unclear short-term market trend made it hard to attract the more speculative investors into the soybean market.
"Investors prefer to put their money into the more active stock market for quick profit," one trader said.
China's stock markets in Shanghai and Shenzhen have been trading actively with more and more hot money flowing into them, traders said.
Analysts expect soybeans not to rise or fall sharply in the short term.
